## Change classification

- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Catalog or registry
- [ ] Contract or schema
- [ ] Compatibility
- [ ] Conformance or certification
- [ ] Architecture / ADR
- [ ] Security
- [ ] CI / tooling

## Summary

Describe the problem, the change, and why TSIC should own this integration or conformance concern.

## Authority and compatibility

- [ ] No duplicate execution, authorization, policy, approval, or audit authority is introduced.
- [ ] Agent Platform remains the sole generic consequential execution authority.
- [ ] Identity, tenant, trace, and provenance context are preserved where relevant.
- [ ] Contract compatibility and affected consumers are documented.
- [ ] Breaking changes include migration and deprecation guidance.

## Verification evidence

List exact commands, test results, workflow run links, commit SHAs, and evidence scope. Distinguish reference checks from deployed or production evidence.

- [ ] Relevant local checks pass.
- [ ] CI passes.
- [ ] No checks were skipped or weakened to obtain a green result.

## Documentation and security

- [ ] Normative registries, schemas, fixtures, validators, and docs are consistent.
- [ ] Material architecture changes include an ADR.
- [ ] Historical or superseded material is labelled accurately.
- [ ] No credentials, private keys, customer data, PHI, or restricted operational records are included.
- [ ] Security-sensitive findings were reported privately.
